CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee pain after injury at trampoline park.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who sustained a right knee injury one week ago while at a trampoline park with his wife. He reports hearing a snap and experiencing instant pain while on the trampoline. This was his first time visiting a trampoline park. The pain is localized to the lateral aspect of the right knee. He has taken acetaminophen for pain management without significant relief. He has elevated the knee but has not used ice or heat. He reports a limp when walking but is able to bear weight on the affected leg.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies fever, chills, or systemic symptoms. Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily (for hypertension) - takes most days
2. Metformin 500 mg (for diabetes) - takes daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient does not have a consistent exercise regimen. Denies regular workouts. Denies participation in recreational activities until the recent trampoline park visit. Diet consists of general carbohydrate monitoring without formal calorie or macro counting. No specific diet followed. Does not follow a low-salt diet.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure elevated at 180/80 mmHg.
General: Alert and oriented.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs appreciated.
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Right Knee: Tenderness to palpation on lateral aspect. No tenderness on medial aspect. Ecchymosis and edema noted along lateral aspect. No effusion appreciated. Range of motion present but limited by pain. Gait reveals a slight limp. Able to bear weight with difficulty.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee pain, lateral ligament strain: Start meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling. Refer to physical therapy for strengthening and injury prevention. Further imaging if pain persists. Advised that this is a common injury that typically heals on its own.
2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order echocardiogram. Anticipate possible medication modification if blood pressure control remains inadequate.
3. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Order hemoglobin A1c to assess long-term glycemic control. Order lipid panel to assess need for medication adjustment. Encouraged more frequent blood sugar monitoring (2-3 times daily).
